name: The individual human soul, intellect, and the rejection of Averroism
plain_explanation: Aquinas holds each person has exactly one soul (not three, as some earlier theories held), which is the 'form' of the body, present entirely in every part of it, and created fresh by God for each individual rather than transmitted through the parents (unlike, say, physical traits). Crucially, and against Averroes, each person's intellect is likewise their own, individual and distinct -- not a single impersonal intellect in which all people merely participate. This matters because only individual immortality, not Averroes's shared impersonal intellect, secures the Christian doctrine of personal survival and judgment after death.
precise_definition: Aquinas's doctrine, contra Averroes, that the intellectual part of each human soul is numerically distinct for each individual, immaterial and incorruptible, created directly by God (not transmitted through generation), and hence capable of grounding genuine personal immortality.
why_it_mattered: This is the doctrinal crux of the Averroist controversy at thirteenth-century Paris, and Aquinas's decisive rejection of the single-intellect view was central to the Church's condemnation of Latin Averroism.
historical_origin: Developed in Book II of the Summa contra Gentiles as part of Aquinas's broader account of the soul.
examples: The objection Aquinas considers and dismisses as merely 'specious': that if the soul is created afresh rather than transmitted with the semen, an illegitimately conceived child's ensoulment seems to implicate God as an 'accomplice in adultery'
Russell's aside that Aquinas does not discuss the harder, related problem (which troubled Saint Augustine) of how, if each soul is created fresh, it can inherit Adam's original sin
objections: Russell's own view, stated directly, that 'the De Anima leads much more naturally to the view of Averroes than to that of Aquinas'
competing_positions: Averroes's view that intellect is one and impersonal, shared across all human beings
influence_on_later_thinkers: Secured the Church's decisive rejection of Averroism as heretical, shaping subsequent Catholic psychology and eschatology.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Underwrites the doctrine of personal judgment and individual salvation.
